codes.summary: An 'after' names a step written further down the flow, or names the statement it is on.
A call is cancelled after this body already waited for it, so there is nothing left to stop.
A '<-' carries a value where there is no 'repeat' to carry it into.
A second 'wait' or 'drain' on something this body already holds for.
A repeat carries the same name twice.
A repeat is given a second stop condition.
An 'until' or 'while' ends a 'repeat', and there is none here.
A carry names something other than what its repeat carries.
A number the language cannot read.
A count that is not a number of anything: 'parallel 0', 'skip -1'.
Two flows in one file are declared with the same name.
A port is declared twice in one direction.
A number carrying a suffix that is not one of the duration units.
'headers' without the 'forward' that owns it.
Making a node takes parentheses: 'node()' or 'node(id)'.
'stream' or 'required' is written in front of the port's type instead of after it.
A stage is missing the argument it takes, or was given one of the wrong kind.
A function call naming something that is not one of the language's fixed functions.
A pipeline stage the language does not have.
'fail' names something that is not a canonical status code, a number, or a value the flow read.
A port type that is neither built in nor written as a registry tag or a quoted mimetype.
A call used where one of its ports was meant.
'it' outside the 'where', 'map' or 'group' stage whose value it names.
A status asked of something that has none.
Something that is not a call is asked to stop.
Something that cannot be read is used as a pipeline source.
A stream is written somewhere that cannot be written: an 'in' port, a call's output, a barrier.
A name is bound twice in one scope.
A name nothing has bound, including one bound further down: a flow reads in order.
A node map used before 'nodes' declares it.
A port the action being called does not declare.
A sequence of stages that cannot produce what it appears to: dropping from one value, counting a reduced stream, 'first 0'.
A stage with nothing to do: choosing between the single value a reducing stage left, or the same reshaping twice.
A counted 'skip' applied to something that is not a port or a node; '| drop n' is the one that drops from a pipeline.
An expression where the grammar requires a constant.
More text after a complete statement; one statement per line.
A flow, block, call, list or object that is never closed.
Text where the grammar expects something else.
A character the language has no meaning for anywhere.
A string that is not closed before its line ends.
A barrier bound to a name nothing reads; the flow still waits there, so the name is the dead part.
A header declared under an alias nothing uses.
A 'for' variable no pass of the loop reads.
A node map nothing is placed in.
An 'out' port nothing in the flow writes, so a caller reading it gets nothing.
A 'try' whose status nothing reads: a failure leaves the ports it feeds silently empty.
